title: Colossal Biosciences announces new AI platform to help accelerate de-extinction efforts
key_facts: Colossal Biosciences announced GenoMorph, an AI platform, on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026 (TechCrunch exclusive).
It uses 3D morphology, comparative genomics and developmental biology to find genes to edit in species with little gene data, starting with the dodo.
Colossal has one dodo genome versus about 100 for its woolly mammoth project.
Trained on developmental data from chickens, quail, ducks and pigeons plus genetic information and 3D skull measurements from 70+ bird species; took over a year to build.
It has identified about 2,300 promising DNA editing targets for dodo skull and face shape, still to be tested in the lab.
Colossal's Nicobar pigeon colony now has 36 birds and it created cells that become eggs and sperm.
CEO Ben Lamm says the tool does not edit genes and an edit is not assumed safe; Peter Diamandis launched NeoGenesis Capital to back Colossal-platform companies.
quote_evidence: The platform, called GenoMorph, uses advanced 3D morphology, comparative genomics, and developmental biology to identify genes that could be edited in de-extinction projects with limited gene data.
“So far we’ve identified approximately 2,300 promising DNA editing targets for the dodo cranial facial morphology that we can now test in the lab,” he continued.
“Identifying a potential edit doesn’t mean we immediately introduce it into an animal or assume it’s safe,” he continued.
why_it_matters_hint: An example of AI narrowing a huge search for genes, though the targets are predictions not yet tested.
notes: Company claims relayed by TechCrunch; the 2,300 targets are predictions awaiting lab tests.
